texts: bad: all three parts of the opening frame land outside what our instruction set licenses - 'late summer' becomes a loose symbol in the time slot that does not compose with Year 1, 'the first night of her apprenticeship' puts a night object where a time value belongs (so a 'when?' question returns a thing, not a time), and 'first' is ranked on no stated ordering. Rewrite as: 'During the late summer of Year 1, during the first night of her apprenticeship, Coraline Ash did not light the lantern.' - 'during' nests one period inside another, which is a licensed carrier, so both frames become real periods the denial hangs on and Year 1 attaches to the summer. The definite 'the lantern' also introduces it outside the denial, which makes its link to the lantern Pell tends in sentences 4-7 certain rather than left to our discretion. The rank 'first' is the remaining residue - it is recorded, but on an ordering the sentence never names.
good. the walk keeps Cliff Path as a named path, Pell as a companion in the walking rather than a means, and sundown and dawn as the interval endpoints.
good. the case is typed as a leather case that is also a case, and Pell is attached as its owner rather than as something it is a part of.
good. the glass comes out as a part of the lantern and cleaning marks it as changed; the definite 'the lantern' reuses the lantern from sentence 1 instead of minting a second one.
good. same shape as the previous sentence - the wick is a part of the same lantern, and trimming takes it as the thing changed.
good. the reservoir is a part of the same lantern, mire-essence is typed as a kind of essence, and it lands as the substance the filling was done with.
good. a separate lighting event on the same lantern, kept distinct from the lighting denied in sentence 1.

mixed: 'the steps' comes out as a bare group of steps with nothing tying it to the four things Pell just did, so 'which steps did she write down?' returns an empty group - the link you intend is a bridging inference we are not allowed to add. Rewrite as: 'Coraline Ash wrote Pell's steps in a notebook.' - the possessive at least attaches the group to Pell; if you need the four actions themselves recoverable, name them in the sentence.
